items.stem: A Statement of Actuarial Opinion on loss reserves primarily addresses whether the reserves are:

options.text: Reasonable and make adequate provision for unpaid claims
options.rationale: Correct: the opinion speaks to reasonableness and adequacy of reserves.
The opinion is about reasonableness, not minimization.
Reserves are not set equal to premium income.
Reserve adequacy is central to solvency.

items.explanation: Correct: the opinion speaks to reasonableness and adequacy of reserves.

items.stem: Select TWO mechanisms that support policyholder protection when a US insurer becomes insolvent.

options.rationale: Correct: guaranty funds cover certain claims of insolvent insurers.

options.text: Risk-based capital (RBC) requirements and regulatory action levels
options.rationale: Correct: RBC triggers regulatory intervention before insolvency worsens.

options.text: Letting the insurer set its own solvency rules with no oversight
options.rationale: Self-regulation without oversight does not protect policyholders.

options.text: Deleting the insurer’s reserves from the balance sheet
options.rationale: Removing reserves would harm, not protect, policyholders.

options.text: Paying dividends ahead of claims in insolvency
options.rationale: Policyholder claims rank ahead of shareholder dividends.

items.explanation: Correct: guaranty funds cover certain claims of insolvent insurers.
